background_notes.fact: For a finite positive dimension n, a compact C⊂R^n is closed. If R>0 and C⊂(-R,R)^n, then Q=[-R,R]^n is compact, int Q=(-R,R)^n contains C, and its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. Consequently (R^n\C)×int J is open.

grounds.reason: A positive finite real radius with strict box containment has been proved.
Q is the closed box defined from that radius.

background_notes.justification: Compact sets in Hausdorff Euclidean space are closed: separating a point outside the compact set from its points and taking a finite subcover gives an exterior neighborhood. A finite product of closed bounded intervals is compact; R>0 makes its interior the product of the open intervals. The rectangle formula for finite-dimensional Lebesgue measure gives the product of the n side lengths, (2R)^n, which is finite. Complements of closed sets and products of open sets are open.

background_notes.fact: If a smooth map on an open subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space equals a constant on an open subregion, then all positive-order partial derivatives vanish on that subregion. Thus, on (R^n\C)×int J, e and every derivative product in N002, including e_t and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), vanish.

grounds.reason: u is jointly smooth on the open spacetime domain.
The exterior-interior spacetime subregion is open and contained in the domain.
The derivatives and dot products have their classical meanings.
e is a finite sum of squared first derivatives.

background_notes.justification: At each point of the open constant region, sufficiently small coordinate increments stay in it, so componentwise first difference quotients vanish. Repeating locally on the resulting zero derivative functions gives all higher partial derivatives. The density and indicated products are zero throughout that open region since their derivative factors vanish; their indicated derivatives are also zero by the same locality argument.

background_notes.fact: For smooth u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m with finite positive n,m, all scalar expressions listed in N002 are continuous on the spacetime domain. At every fixed r∈int J they are continuous and Borel measurable on R^n, and their absolute values are bounded on compact Q.

grounds.reason: All coordinate sums and dot products have finitely many terms.
Every derivative needed in the listed expressions exists and is continuous.
The scalar expressions use the explicit Euclidean dot products and finite-square-sum density.
The slice is taken at a fixed positive time r.

background_notes.justification: Derivatives of a smooth map are smooth; finite sums and products of smooth scalar components are smooth. This includes e_t and the derivative of the indicated dot product. Restriction along the continuous spatial slice preserves continuity. Continuous real functions are Borel measurable, and the continuous image of a compact set under their absolute value is compact in R and hence bounded (empty-set boundedness is immediate).

background_notes.fact: If a real continuous function f on R^n vanishes outside C⊂Q, Q is a measurable set of finite Lebesgue measure, and |f|≤M on Q for some finite M≥0, then f is Lebesgue integrable and ∫_{R^n}|f|≤M|Q|. This applies separately to every scalar function listed in N002 at each r∈int J.

grounds.reason: Q is a compact box of finite measure, contains C, and the relevant derivatives vanish outside C.
e,e_t and all listed derivative products vanish outside C at interior times.
Each function is continuous, measurable, and has a finite bound on Q at the chosen time.

background_notes.justification: Continuity gives Lebesgue measurability. Increase the absolute bound to be nonnegative. Since f vanishes outside C⊂Q, |f|≤M1_Q everywhere. Monotonicity of the nonnegative Lebesgue integral and the integral of an indicator give ∫|f|≤Mμ(Q)<∞, which is precisely absolute integrability. The bound may depend on the function and the fixed time, as allowed by N002.
